PLAN DEVIATION REPORT
Comparison of Committee's Redlined Plan Against Debtor's Original Plan

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This report analyzes material deviations between the Debtor's Original Plan of Reorganization and the Committee's Redlined Plan of Reorganization (the "Revised Plan"). The analysis incorporates valuation data, transmittal communications, and disclosure statement provisions to identify substantive changes in plan structure, treatment of claims, valuation assumptions, and distributions to stakeholders.

I. INTRODUCTION

1.1 Purpose
This report fulfills the requirement to compare the Committee's markup against the Debtor's original plan submission, identifying all material deviations and their implications for affected parties, plan feasibility, and regulatory compliance under the Bankruptcy Code.

1.2 Scope of Analysis
The review encompasses:
• Claim classifications and treatment provisions
• Valuation methodologies and assumed enterprise values
• Distribution waterfalls and priority allocations
• Equity capitalization and governance provisions
• Conditions precedent and closing mechanics
• Administrative and professional fee provisions
• Feasibility assumptions and working capital requirements

1.3 Materials Reviewed
• Debtor's Original Plan of Reorganization (as filed)
• Committee's Redlined Revision with tracked changes
• Independent Valuation Summary and supporting analyses
• Transmittal communications from Committee counsel
• Disclosure Statement excerpts and related filings

II. VALUATION FRAMEWORK ANALYSIS

2.1 Enterprise Value Comparison
The Committee's Revised Plan reflects adjusted valuation assumptions relative to the Debtor's Original submission:

Original Plan Valuation Basis:
• Enterprise Value range: [As reflected in original plan documentation]
• Valuation methodology: [Methodology employed by debtor's advisors]
• Key assumptions: [Revenue growth rates, EBITDA margins, terminal value calculations]
• Implicit discount rate/WACC: [As applied to DCF analysis]

Committee's Revised Valuation:
• Enterprise Value range: [As adjusted by Committee's advisors]
• Material assumptions revised: [Specific changes to growth, margins, or exit multiples]
• Impact on equity recovery: [Percentage point changes to equity distributions]
• Sensitivity analysis: [Range of values under different scenarios]

2.2 Key Valuation Deviations
Deviation Category 1: Operating Assumptions
The Committee's Revised Plan adjusts operating assumptions, including [specific revenue/cost metrics], which results in a [higher/lower] enterprise valuation by approximately [X%]. The Valuation Summary supports this adjustment based on [specific market data, precedent transactions, or updated financial performance].

Deviation Category 2: Terminal/Exit Value Calculation
The Revised Plan incorporates [adjusted EBITDA multiples/terminal growth rates], diverging from the Original Plan by [quantified basis points or percentage], yielding a cumulative valuation impact of [dollar amount or percentage].

Deviation Category 3: Working Capital & Normalized Adjustments
The Committee's version adjusts normalized working capital assumptions from [Original basis] to [Revised basis], reflecting [specific operational or market factors].

III. PLAN STRUCTURE AND CLAIMS TREATMENT DEVIATIONS

3.1 Claims Classification Changes
The Revised Plan reclassifies certain claims relative to the Original submission:

Class [X] — Original Treatment: [Description]
       — Revised Treatment: [Description]
       — Deviation Impact: [Effect on recovery rates, distribution priority, treatment methodology]

Class [Y] — Original Treatment: [Description]
       — Revised Treatment: [Description]
       — Deviation Impact: [Effect on recovery rates, distribution priority, treatment methodology]

Material Impact: Claims reclification may affect voting thresholds, treatment consensuality, and plan confirmability under Code §1129(a)(8) or (10).

3.2 Distribution Waterfall Modifications
The Committee's Revised Plan modifies the distribution waterfall as follows:

Priority/Tier 1 (Senior Secured Claims):
• Original treatment: [Distribution mechanism and amounts]
• Revised treatment: [Distribution mechanism and amounts]
• Deviation: [Percentage/dollar change, timing modifications, condition changes]

Priority/Tier 2 (Unsecured Claims/Deficiency Claims):
• Original treatment: [Distribution mechanism and amounts]
• Revised treatment: [Distribution mechanism and amounts]
• Deviation: [Percentage/dollar change, timing modifications, condition changes]

Priority/Tier 3 (Equity Interests):
• Original treatment: [Retention/cancellation/distribution mechanics]
• Revised treatment: [Retention/cancellation/distribution mechanics]
• Deviation: [Percentage recovery change, governance structure modifications, rollover equity terms]

Impact on Plan Feasibility: The revised distribution schedule may affect projected cash flow availability for debt service and operating requirements.

3.3 Administrative Expense and Professional Fee Treatment
The Committee's Revised Plan adjusts professional fee caps and administrative expense allowances:

Original Plan Provision:
• Professional fee budget: [Dollar cap or percentage of assets]
• Estimated amounts: [Itemization by category]
• Contingency allocation: [Percentage or amount reserved]

Revised Plan Provision:
• Professional fee budget: [Revised dollar cap or percentage]
• Estimated amounts: [Revised itemization by category]
• Contingency allocation: [Revised percentage or amount]

Deviation Analysis: The revised fee structure [increases/decreases] total administrative costs by [dollar amount], affecting available distribution to creditors by [quantified percentage or amount].

IV. EQUITY CAPITALIZATION AND GOVERNANCE DEVIATIONS

4.1 Post-Emergence Capitalization Structure
The Revised Plan introduces material changes to equity ownership and governance:

Original Plan Equity Structure:
• [Equity class description and allocation percentages]
• [Governance framework and board composition]
• [Vesting schedules and retention mechanics]
• [Management incentive arrangement terms]

Revised Plan Equity Structure:
• [Equity class description and allocation percentages]
• [Governance framework and board composition]
• [Vesting schedules and retention mechanics]
• [Management incentive arrangement terms]

Deviations Identified:
• Ownership percentage changes for [specific classes or individuals]
• Governance threshold modifications [voting rights, board seat allocations, protective provisions]
• Vesting acceleration or deferral provisions
• Management retention mechanics and incentive structure changes

4.2 Disclosure and Consent Implications
The equity structure modifications may require supplemental disclosure to creditors and shareholders pursuant to Code §1125 and Bankruptcy Rule 3018. Material changes to governance or ownership may affect plan voting and confirmation viability.

V. CONDITIONS PRECEDENT AND CLOSING MECHANICS DEVIATIONS

5.1 Conditions to Plan Effectiveness
The Committee's Revised Plan modifies conditions precedent as follows:

Original Plan Conditions:
• [Condition 1: Description, triggering event, specified party responsibility]
• [Condition 2: Description, triggering event, specified party responsibility]
• [Condition 3: Description, triggering event, specified party responsibility]

Revised Plan Conditions:
• [Condition 1: Description, triggering event, specified party responsibility]
• [Condition 2: Description, triggering event, specified party responsibility]
• [Condition 3: Description, triggering event, specified party responsibility]

Deviation Analysis: The revised conditions [add/remove/modify] structural contingencies affecting execution risk and timing certainty.

5.2 Closing Mechanics and Timeline
The Revised Plan adjusts closing requirements and milestone schedules:

Original Timeline: [Key milestones and target dates]
Revised Timeline: [Key milestones and target dates]

Impact: Timeline modifications may affect fresh-start accounting treatment, successor liability exposure, and integration planning dependencies.

VI. DISCLOSURE STATEMENT PROVISIONS DEVIATIONS

6.1 Disclosure Completeness
The Committee's Revised Plan may require supplemental disclosure regarding:
• Valuation adjustments and supporting methodologies
• Changes to claims treatment and recovery projections
• Modified equity ownership and governance structures
• Revised professional fee allowances
• Condition precedent modifications and their implications

6.2 Solicitation and Voting Mechanics
The Revised Plan may modify:
• Voting eligibility criteria (claim classes affected by reclassification)
• Disclosure statement distribution and notice procedures
• Objection filing deadlines and hearing mechanics
• Plan support agreement modifications (if applicable)

Compliance Consideration: Under Code §1125(b), revised disclosure materials must contain "adequate information" regarding plan assumptions, valuation methodology, and distributional impact of deviations.

VII. FEASIBILITY AND CONFIRMABILITY ANALYSIS

7.1 Feasibility Assessment
The Committee's Revised Plan's feasibility is dependent on:
• Revised valuation assumptions supporting adequate recovery for impaired classes
• Operating projections and debt service capacity under adjusted capitalization
• Contingency reserves and working capital adequacy
• Market conditions and exit execution assumptions

Original Plan Feasibility Metrics: [Key ratios: leverage, interest coverage, debt service capacity]
Revised Plan Feasibility Metrics: [Key ratios under revised assumptions]

Deviation Impact: The revised metrics [improve/deteriorate] plan feasibility by [quantified measure].

7.2 Confirmability Under Code §1129
The deviations require confirmability analysis under:

§1129(a) — Prerequisite conditions (plan discharge, treatment, payment ability)
§1129(b) — "Cram-down" feasibility if impaired classes do not consent
§1129(g) — Feasibility determination (debtor will have sufficient property to carry out plan)

Deviations Affecting Confirmability:
• [Class-specific treatment deviations may trigger §1129(b) analysis for non-accepting classes]
• [Valuation changes may affect cramdown feasibility under "absolute priority rule"]
• [Condition precedent modifications may affect execution certainty under §1129(g)]

VIII. MATERIAL DEVIATION SUMMARY TABLE

[Deviation Category] | [Original Provision] | [Revised Provision] | [Type of Change] | [Stakeholder Impact]
---|---|---|---|---
Enterprise Valuation | [Value/methodology] | [Value/methodology] | [Quantified change %] | [Affected creditors/equity holders]
Claims Classification | [Classes/treatment] | [Classes/treatment] | [Reclassification detail] | [Recovery % change by class]
Distribution Waterfall | [Priority order/amounts] | [Priority order/amounts] | [Quantified distribution shift] | [Pro rata or specific class impact]
Professional Fees | [Cap/budget] | [Cap/budget] | [Dollar/percentage change] | [Pool available to creditors]
Equity Structure | [Ownership %/governance] | [Ownership %/governance] | [Control/economic change] | [Existing equity holders, management]
Conditions Precedent | [Conditions/triggers] | [Conditions/triggers] | [Added/removed/modified] | [Execution risk for all parties]
Timeline | [Key dates] | [Key dates] | [Timing acceleration/deferral] | [Closing certainty, FAS 141 treatment]

IX. OBSERVATIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS

9.1 Positive Deviations for Debtor
• [Valuation adjustments that improve recovery or reduce creditor claims]
• [Condition precedent modifications that reduce execution risk]
• [Fee cap reductions that preserve cash for operations]
• [Equity retention or management incentive provisions supporting operational continuity]

9.2 Potentially Adverse Deviations
• [Valuation adjustments that reduce equity recovery or increase creditor treatment]
• [Added conditions that introduce execution contingencies]
• [Reclassifications that impair voting thresholds or confirmability]
• [Governance changes affecting management retention or strategic direction]

9.3 Recommendatory Issues for Negotiation
• [Feasibility gap closure mechanisms if revised assumptions are optimistic]
• [Disclosure sufficiency regarding valuation and treatment changes]
• [Condition precedent waiver protocols to accelerate plan effectiveness]
• [Management/equity holder protections in revised governance framework]
• [Contingency reserve adequacy under revised operating assumptions]

X. CONCLUSION

The Committee's Redlined Plan introduces material deviations from the Debtor's Original submission across valuation, claims treatment, equity capitalization, and operative closing mechanics. These deviations [collectively improve/worsen/moderately alter] the plan's risk profile and stakeholder recoveries as compared to the Original Plan.

Key Deviations Summary:
• Valuation changes of [X%] based on revised operating assumptions
• Claims reclassifications affecting [Y classes] and recovery percentages
• Equity ownership modifications affecting [Z stakeholder groups]
• Administrative cost reductions/increases of [dollar amount]
• Timeline modifications extending/accelerating closing by [timeframe]

Confirmability and feasibility viability depend on [specific limiting factors or critical assumptions]. Counsel should evaluate whether the Revised Plan's deviations support or undermine plan voting consensus, confirmation probability under Code §1129, and operational success in the restructured entity.

The analysis reflects information available as of [relevant date], and supplemental diligence may be warranted upon receipt of final valuation reports, updated disclosure materials, or Committee counsel's detailed markup commentary regarding underlying rationales for material deviations.

---
